168	// severityTokens are the four cumulative severity filters (Rule 136).
169	//
170	// They replaced a cycle on `.` — which also cost the table its sort key. A
171	// cycle can only ask "at least this severe", and the question actually asked is
172	// "CRITICAL and HIGH", which is not a threshold: it excludes MEDIUM while
173	// including CRITICAL. Four toggles can say it and a cycle never could.
174	func severityTokens() []sharedcomponents.FilterToken {
175		return []sharedcomponents.FilterToken{
176			{Label: "critical"}, {Label: "high"}, {Label: "medium"}, {Label: "low"},
177		}
178	}
179	
180	// severityToken maps a finding's severity onto its token label. UNKNOWN has no
181	// token, so it is only ever hidden by an explicit choice of others.
182	var severityToken = REDACTED
183		scan.SeverityCritical: "critical",
184		scan.SeverityHigh:     "high",
185		scan.SeverityMedium:   "medium",
186		scan.SeverityLow:      "low",
187	}
188	
189	// matchesSeverity keeps everything while no token is active: an empty filter
190	// means "no opinion", not "nothing".
191	func matchesSeverity(f scan.Finding, active map[string]bool) bool {
192		if len(active) == 0 {
193			return true
194		}
195		return active[severityToken[f.Severity]]
196	}

198	// NewWithPreloadedResult creates a security view showing a stored scan result.
199	// Used to display cached results without re-scanning (Rule 126).
200	func NewWithPreloadedResult(cfg *config.Config, secrets credentials.Storage, result *scan.Result) Model {
201		m := New(cfg, secrets)
202		m.state = StateResults
203		m.result = result
204		m.targetPath = result.Target
205		m.targetLabel = labelForResult(cfg, result)
206		m.activeTab = TabCVE
207		// Filled here rather than waiting for the first WindowSizeMsg: the rows do
208		// not depend on the width any more, so nothing was gained by deferring and
209		// the table was empty until the terminal happened to report its size.
210		m.updateFindingsTable()
211		return m
212	}

215	// filters the user is looking through. It is what a verification re-scan hands
216	// back, so the table stops listing a rule the edit has already dealt with.
217	func (m *Model) setResult(result *scan.Result) {
218		m.result = result
219		m.targetPath = result.Target
220		m.targetLabel = labelForResult(m.config, result)
221		m.updateFindingsTable()

228		// than the branch that would decide not to.
229		return loadInventoryCmd(m.ciForgeURL())
230	}

232	// InEditMode reports whether a field or a modal has the keyboard, which is what
233	// stops the router claiming ":", "q" and "?" for itself.
234	//
235	// The results and details states used to be listed here too, for one reason: it
236	// was the only way to be handed esc. The router forwards esc unconditionally now
237	// (§1.3 D15), so those states are ordinary again — and get the command line, the
238	// help overlay and quit back with them.
239	func (m Model) InEditMode() bool {
240		switch {
241		case m.confirmModal != nil, m.scanAllModal != nil:
242			return true
243		case m.state == StateInventory:
244			return m.inventory.InEditMode()
245		case m.state == StateResults:
246			// The findings table gained a filter bar with the severity tokens, so
247			// this state has a focused field to declare like any other.
248			return m.findingsTable.InEditMode()
249		}
250		return false
251	}

52		}

54		// screen, and the entry used to appear and disappear as the cursor crossed
55		// a Trivy secret in a list holding both tools' findings.

57		// findings does not reach it, so those keys are greyed there and S — which
58		// means nothing on the four tabs of findings — is the one that lights up.
59		notFindings := m.activeTab == TabRemediation
60		// Enter opens the selected finding, or on the Remediation tab the diff of the
61		// chosen bases: one key, the same place in the column, a different verb.

67		// writes is the tab's. The label changes with it so the column never

74			{Key: "tab", Description: "Switch tab"},

134	// GetHeaderInfo returns the key-value info for the header: the context, one
135	// count, and in the results how much of it is fixable.
136	//
137	// It used to carry seven fields in the results state, which is exactly the
138	// number buildInfoLines renders — an eighth would have been dropped in silence.
139	// Most of them had stopped earning their line:
140	//
141	//   - Trivy and Gitleaks versions answered "can I scan?", which the dashboard
142	//     already answers from shared.State.Tools, and which an inventory of past
143	//     scans is not about.
144	//   - Filter showed the severity filter, permanently reading ALL, and meaning
145	//     nothing on the Secrets tab or in the details.
146	//   - Secrets and Licenses duplicated the tab bar, which renders the same two
147	//     numbers a line below.
148	//
149	// Fixable came back on its own merits: it is the one figure that says what can
150	// be done, which none of the removed ones did.
151	//
152	// The context is what replaced them, and it is the one thing that was missing:
153	// the scan caches are scoped to a context, so the same inventory rows mean
154	// different things in two of them and look identical.
155	func (m Model) GetHeaderInfo(context string) []shortcut.HeaderInfo {
156		info := []shortcut.HeaderInfo{
157			{Key: "Context", Value: context, Style: theme.HeaderValueStyle},
158		}
159		if key, value, ok := m.headerCount(); ok {
160			info = append(info, shortcut.HeaderInfo{Key: key, Value: value, Style: theme.HeaderValueStyle})
161		}
162		if value, style, ok := m.headerFixable(); ok {
163			info = append(info, shortcut.HeaderInfo{Key: "Fixable", Value: value, Style: style})
164		}
165		if value, ok := m.headerUnrendered(); ok {
166			info = append(info, shortcut.HeaderInfo{Key: "Not rendered", Value: value, Style: theme.HeaderValueStyle})
167		}
168		if sig, ok := m.signatureHeader(); ok {
169			info = append(info, sig)
170		}
171		return info
172	}
173	
174	// headerUnrendered is how many Helm charts and Kustomize overlays the schema
175	// stage could not look at, for want of helm or kustomize (§3.80). Without it a
176	// repository of charts would read as schema-clean when nothing was checked.
177	// Absent when there are none — it is not a count of findings, and a "0" on
178	// every result would be noise about a stage most repositories do not need.
179	func (m Model) headerUnrendered() (string, bool) {
180		if (m.state != StateResults && m.state != StateDetails) || m.result == nil || len(m.result.K8sUnrendered) == 0 {
181			return "", false
182		}
183		return strconv.Itoa(len(m.result.K8sUnrendered)) + " (install helm / kustomize)", true
184	}
185	
186	// headerFixable is how many of the vulnerabilities have a fixed version, split
187	// by what has to move: "12 (8 base, 4 deps)". It is the one number that says
188	// what can be done about the findings, which the count above does not. Like the
189	// count, it is absent where the state is a list of nothing, and it is present
190	// on both sides of the results/details step so the header does not change
191	// under the reader (Rule 130).
192	func (m Model) headerFixable() (string, lipgloss.Style, bool) {
193		if (m.state != StateResults && m.state != StateDetails) || m.result == nil {
194			return "", lipgloss.Style{}, false
195		}
196		s := remediation.Summarize(m.result.Findings)
197		if s.Fixable() == 0 {
198			return "0", theme.DimStyle, true
199		}
200		var parts []string
201		if s.BaseImage > 0 {
202			parts = append(parts, strconv.Itoa(s.BaseImage)+" base")
203		}
204		if s.Dependencies > 0 {
205			parts = append(parts, strconv.Itoa(s.Dependencies)+" deps")
206		}
207		if s.Unclassified > 0 {
208			parts = append(parts, strconv.Itoa(s.Unclassified)+" unclassified")
209		}
210		return strconv.Itoa(s.Fixable()) + " (" + strings.Join(parts, ", ") + ")", theme.HeaderValueStyle, true
211	}
212	
213	// headerCount is the one number the header shows, named for whatever the state
214	// is actually a list of. The form and the scanning screen are lists of nothing,
215	// and report no count rather than a zero.
216	func (m Model) headerCount() (key, value string, ok bool) {
217		switch m.state {
218		case StateInventory:
219			return "Targets", strconv.Itoa(len(m.inventory.Items())), true
220		case StateResults, StateDetails:
221			if m.result == nil {
222				return "", "", false
223			}
224			return "Findings", strconv.Itoa(m.result.TotalFindings()), true
225		}
226		return "", "", false
227	}

16	// ViewState represents the current state of the security view.
17	//
18	// There were five. StateInput was the form, and StateScanning the screen that
19	// ran one scan in place while the user watched it — both went with the form
20	// (phase 3). What replaced them is the inventory, which rescans in the
21	// background with a spinner on the row, so nothing waits on a whole screen.
22	type ViewState int
23	
24	const (
25		StateInventory ViewState = iota // What this context has scanned, read from the caches
26		StateResults                    // Displaying results summary
27		StateDetails                    // Showing detailed findings
28	)
29	
30	// Model represents the security scanner view
31	type Model struct {
32		config *config.Config
33		// secrets is the context's store, used only to load the forge token for a
34		// CI scan. Nothing else here reads a credential.
35		secrets credentials.Storage
36		width   int
37		height  int
38	
39		state  ViewState
40		result *scan.Result
41	
42		// deps is the router's detection of the scanners, nil until it lands.
43		deps *scan.Report
44	
45		// Inventory state
46		inventory datatable.Model[scanTarget]
47	
48		// jobs is the router snapshot of everything running anywhere. See jobs.go:
49		// the rows' activity is derived from it, so there is no in-flight state here
50		// to carry across a reload.
51		jobs []jobs.Run
52	
53		// failures is a copy of the registry's remembered failures, replaced (never
54		// merged) by handleJobsChanged, and contextName the context the snapshot was
55		// built for (ChangedMsg.Context).
56		failures    []jobs.Failure
57		contextName string
58	
59		// inventoryLoading is true while loadInventoryCmd is in flight. It exists
60		// because an empty table and a table that has not answered yet look the
61		// same, and they mean opposite things: "Nothing scanned yet" asserted
62		// before the caches were read is a claim the view cannot make, and the one
63		// the user saw flash by before the list appeared.
64		//
65		// It also drives the shared activity dot (status, WantsBlink).
66		inventoryLoading bool
67

128	// New builds the view. The secret store comes in at construction, like

171	// cycle can only ask "at least this severe", and the question actually asked is
172	// "CRITICAL and HIGH", which is not a threshold: it excludes MEDIUM while
173	// including CRITICAL. Four toggles can say it and a cycle never could.
174	func severityTokens() []sharedcomponents.FilterToken {
175		return []sharedcomponents.FilterToken{
176			{Label: "critical"}, {Label: "high"}, {Label: "medium"}, {Label: "low"},

181	// token, so it is only ever hidden by an explicit choice of others.
182	var severityToken = REDACTED

191	func matchesSeverity(f scan.Finding, active map[string]bool) bool {
192		if len(active) == 0 {

194		}
195		return active[severityToken[f.Severity]]
196	}

215	// filters the user is looking through. It is what a verification re-scan hands
216	// back, so the table stops listing a rule the edit has already dealt with.
217	func (m *Model) setResult(result *scan.Result) {
218		m.result = result

226		// Loaded whatever the opening state: a view opened on a result returns
227		// to the inventory on ctrl+r, and reading two small files is cheaper
228		// than the branch that would decide not to.

232	// InEditMode reports whether a field or a modal has the keyboard, which is what
233	// stops the router claiming ":", "q" and "?" for itself.
234	//
235	// The results and details states used to be listed here too, for one reason: it
236	// was the only way to be handed esc. The router forwards esc unconditionally now
237	// (§1.3 D15), so those states are ordinary again — and get the command line, the
238	// help overlay and quit back with them.
239	func (m Model) InEditMode() bool {

249		}
